title: 5–15 February - 54th Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 54th annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from 5–15 February 2004. The festival opened with out of competition film Cold Mountain by Anthony Minghella.

title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2004
text: Germany was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 2004 with the song "Can't Wait Until Tonight", written by Stefan Raab, and performed by Max. The German participating broadcaster on behalf of ARD, Norddeutscher Rundfunk, organised the national final Germany 12 Points!
wiki: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2004

title: 2004 Cologne bombing
text: On 9 June 2004, a nail bomb detonated in Cologne, Germany, in a business area popular with immigrants from Turkey. Twenty-two people were wounded, with four sustaining serious injuries.

title: Protests against Hartz IV reforms
text: The Protests against Hartz IV reforms in Germany were aimed at the 2004 Hartz IV reform, which provide significant cutbacks in social welfare benefits for long-term unemployed persons. The demonstrations started on 2 August, when about 10,000 people took part.

title: The Berlin Rules on Water Resources are adopted by the International Law Association.
text: The Berlin Rules on Water Resources is a document adopted by the International Law Association to summarize international law customarily applied in modern times to freshwater resources, whether within a nation or crossing international boundaries. title: The Far Right National Democratic Party of Germany (NPD) won 12 seats in the 2004 Saxony state election. This is the first time since the 1960s that the party had seats in a state parliament.
text: The 2004 Saxony state election was held on 19 September 2004 to elect the members of the 4th Landtag of Saxony. The incumbent Christian Democratic Union government led by Minister-President Georg Milbradt lost its majority.

title: Several thousands of Germans are among thousands of people killed by the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.
text: Germans are the natives or inhabitants of Germany, or sometimes more broadly any people who are of German descent or native speakers of the German language. The constitution of Germany, implemented in 1949 following the end of World War II, defines a German as a German citizen.

title: 2003–04 Deutsche Eishockey Liga season
text: The 2003–04 Deutsche Eishockey Liga season was the 10th season since the founding of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga. The Frankfurt Lions became German Champions, and the Wölfe Freiburg (Freiburg Wolves) were relegated back to the 2.

title: 2004 German motorcycle Grand Prix
text: The 2004 German motorcycle Grand Prix was the eighth round of the 2004 MotoGP Championship. It took place on the weekend of 16–18 July 2004 at the Sachsenring.

title: “Shut Up” by The Black Eyed Peas
text: "Shut Up" is a song by American hip-hop group the Black Eyed Peas for their third studio album Elephunk. Lyrically, it is about a disastrous courtship with the chorus consisting of the lines "Shut up, just shut up, shut up".
listen: Shut Up The Black Eyed Peas

title: “Du hast mein Herz gebrochen” by Yvonne Catterfeld
text: "Du hast mein Herz gebrochen" is a song by German singer Yvonne Catterfeld. It was written by Dieter Bohlen and Eko Fresh, and produced by the former for Catterfeld's second studio album, Farben meiner Welt (2004).
listen: Du hast mein Herz gebrochen Yvonne Catterfeld

title: “Augen auf!” by Oomph!
text: "Augen auf!" is the first single from the German industrial metal group Oomph!'s album Wahrheit oder Pflicht, and their first released under the GUN label. It is often considered the best-known Oomph!

title: “Just One Last Dance” by 15 March
text: "Just One Last Dance" is a song by German recording artist Sarah Connor. It was written and produced by Kay Denar and Rob Tyger for her third studio album, Key to My Soul.

title: “Can't Wait Until Tonight” by 22 March
text: "Can't Wait Until Tonight" was the German entry in the Eurovision Song Contest 2004, performed in English and Turkish by Maximilian Mutzke. The song was written and composed by Stefan Raab, who previously had written both Guildo Horn's 1998 entry "Guildo hat euch lieb!" and his own "Wadde hadde dudde da?" in 2000.

title: “Yeah!” by Usher featuring Ludacris and Lil' Jon
text: "Yeah!" is a song by American singer Usher featuring American rappers Lil Jon and Ludacris. The song is written by the featured artists alongside Sean Garrett, J. Que, Robert McDowell, and LRoc, and is produced by Lil Jon.
listen: Yeah! Usher featuring Ludacris and Lil' Jon

title: “I Don't Wanna Know” by 10 May
text: "I Don't Wanna Know" is a song by American singer Mario Winans, featuring American rapper P. Diddy and Irish singer Enya. The song is based on a sample of the Fugees' song "Ready or Not", which in turn samples the synthesizer riff from Enya's song "Boadicea".

title: “Fuck It (I Don't Want You Back)” by 17 May
text: "Fuck It", known as "I Don't Want You Back" for the clean version, is a song by American singer-songwriter Eamon, released as his debut single. The song was co-written by Eamon, Kirk Robinson, and Mark Passy.
wiki: Fuck It (I Don't Want You Back)
listen: Fuck It (I Don't Want You Back) 17 May

title: “Dragostea Din Tei” by O-Zone
text: "Dragostea din tei" is a song recorded by Moldovan group O-Zone, released in Romania around June 2003 by Media Services as the lead single from their third studio album DiscO-Zone (2003). It was written by the band's founder Dan Balan and produced by Bogdan Popoiag.

title: “Obsesión” by Aventura
text: "Obsesión" is a song by Dominican-American bachata band Aventura with Judy Santos as the female vocalist. It was included on their second studio album, We Broke the Rules (2002), and an English-language version was made for the same album.

title: “Call on Me” by Eric Prydz
text: "Call on Me" is a song by the Swedish DJ and producer Eric Prydz, released on 13 September 2004. It is based on a replayed sample of the 1982 Steve Winwood song "Valerie", and was inspired by a similar track created by the French duo Together.

title: “Living to Love You” by Sarah Connor
text: "Living to Love You" is a song by German singer–songwriter Sarah Connor from her fourth studio album, Naughty but Nice. It was written and produced by Rob Tyger and Kay Denar and released as the album's lead single on 8 November 2004.
listen: Living to Love You Sarah Connor

title: “Sweetest Poison” by 27 December
text: "Sweetest Poison" is a song by short-lived German pop band Nu Pagadi. After winning the fourth series of German reality television show Popstars in 2004, Nu Pagadi recorded "Sweetest Poison" and released it as their debut single on 13 December 2004.
